answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by forcing agents to evaluate non-parallelizable sequential puzzles. Rather than spawning swarms across a digital tundra, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated processor time and electrical power per identity. Amid the sable background of bot traffic, each valid node presents a cryptographic pearl of elapsed computation. A key limitation is that custom ASICs allow adversaries to evaluate delay steps faster than standard hardware.
